text: AGR 16
¶ 𒀀𒂵𒊑𒅔, agarin. MOTHER.
𒁹 𒀀𒂵𒊑𒅔 . # . 𒌝𒈬.—Syl. 192.
In another copy #.
This singular word is found in the following passage:
𒄿𒈾 𒈜 𒅁𒁀 𒀀𒂵𒊑𒅔𒉌
𒀀𒀖𒋾𒅀, ina lib ibba agarinni alatti-ya ; in the fair body
of the mother who bore me.—38 BM 3.
¶ 𒀀𒃵𒊑, 𒀀𒄖𒌫𒊑, 𒀀𒄥𒊑, aguri,
agurri, ob. BURNT BRICK.
-i-na a-gam-ri ar-zi
var. -ar-zip-
𒄿𒈾 𒀀𒃵𒊑 𒅈𒍢𒅁, var. 𒅈𒍦,
ina aguri arẓip ; in brick I built.—Tig. viii. 6.
𒊭 𒄿𒈾 𒀀𒃵𒊑 𒊏𒀾𒁍, sa ina aguri raspu ;
which of brick were built.—Tig. vi. 11. See also vi. 19, &c.
𒀀𒄖𒌫𒊑.—E.I.H. iv. 12 ; vi. 51. Birs ii. 3.
𒀀𒄥𒊑 .—Birs i. 25. E.I.H. iii. 16, 69. Porter’s transcript
of vi. 51.
Agurri differs from liban, which is sun-dried only.
𒀀𒄥𒊑𒐁 , aguris ; made of brick. 𒈠𒆷𒀝
𒂍 𒀀𒄥𒊑𒐁 𒈠𒊑𒂊 𒌑𒁀𒀭𒉏,
malak bit aguris mare . . . . . ubannū ; avenue of house in brick,
conspicuous . . . . . I built.—E.I.H. iii. 56. Porter’s transcript is
𒀀𒄥𒊑𒐁, agurris ; he has also 𒈠𒆷𒆪 instead of
malak. See Ezek. xlii. 4 ; in Septuagint περίπατος.
¶ 𒀀𒃼𒌅, 𒀀𒃼𒋾, agartu, agarti ; VALUABLE. Heb. אָגוֹרָה,
a piece of silver, 1 Sam. ii. 36. Dr. Oppert suggests יָקָר, which is better.
𒌑𒉡𒌅 𒆬𒄀 𒆬 𒌓 𒀀𒃼𒌅
𒎏𒋳𒋙, hunutu, ḥuraz, kaspu, agartu, nintaksu ; wealth, gold, silver,
valuables, furniture.—Sen. T. i. 28.
